headline: Strangford oyster growers report the cleanest season since the 2018 closure
standfirst: Improved catchment management upstream has done what eight years of shellfish-water designations could not.

image.alt: Oyster trestles exposed at low water

body.text: Classification results published this week put every sampled bed in the lough at Class A or B, with none downgraded after rainfall events. Growers have spent most of the past decade managing around temporary closures triggered by run-off.
The change is credited to catchment work: fencing watercourses, restoring buffer strips and rebuilding slurry storage on farms well inland of the water itself.
Nobody fixed the lough. They fixed four rivers, and the lough followed.
